feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 6 (track 0.10, body_length 0.10, mass 0.6) is the best design so far at 289.8. Its s-bend and slalom progress rose to 0.181 and 0.191, from 0.127 and 0.093 in iteration 4 (body 0.12, mass 0.7), so shortening the body and reducing mass together helped where track narrowing to 0.09 m did not (iteration 5: 0.132 and 0.091, with oval finish down to 35%). The s-bend and slalom still end off_track at max_error about 0.062 to 0.065, and body_width cannot help because the off-track limit is already at its 0.06 m floor across the allowed range. Oval steering_oscillation in iteration 6 was 0.216, close to the 0.25 threshold. Decide the next change from the race. If s-bend and slalom progress rise above 0.13 with max_error near 0.06 m, the mass lever is working, so keep going down in mass. If progress does not move from iteration 6, mass is not the limit and the next lever is the sensor lead. If the oval finish rate drops below 55% or oscillation exceeds 0.25, the robot is over-responding and the lighter mass needs a lower sensor lead.
requested_changes: If s-bend or slalom progress rises above 0.19 with max_error near 0.06 m at mass 0.5 kg, keep track 0.10 m and body_length 0.10 m, and try mass 0.4 kg (the contract minimum). Evidence: iteration 6 (mass 0.6) gave s-bend 0.181 and slalom 0.191 progress, against 0.127 and 0.093 at mass 0.7 in iteration 4, so mass is the main remaining lever.

If s-bend and slalom progress stay at about 0.18 and 0.19 at mass 0.5 kg, or the oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25, move every sensor y from 0.05 to 0.03 with x and the other geometry fixed. Evidence: oval oscillation was 0.216 in iteration 6 and 0.275 in iteration 1 at a longer lead, so a shorter sensor lead is the next step for both cases.

If the oval finish rate falls below 55% with line loss still zero, return mass to 0.6 kg and keep the 0.10 m track and 0.10 m body. Evidence: iteration 6 gave a 65% oval finish at mass 0.6, while iteration 5 fell to 35% when the track was narrowed to 0.09 m.
